overview:
Illinois's 16th District leans Republican by about eleven points, and incumbent Darin LaHood is seeking another term. He has raised more than $4 million and holds a cash advantage of roughly $6 million over Democrat Paul Nolley, who has about $289,000 on hand. No public general-election polls are available, and no major expert ratings cover the race.

Prediction markets give LaHood roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The district's partisan lean, the incumbent's fundraising edge, and the absence of meaningful outside spending against him all point to a comfortable Republican hold, even if the national environment favors Democrats. Nolley would need a dramatic shift in the political climate to make this competitive.
